scope: Resolve the 0x1B..0x21 unmatched-opcode mystery from the async-producers-catalog pass. Decomp FUN_006125E0 (the sole producer of 0x1B..0x21) and its caller chain to determine why these opcodes have no Element class consumer.

method.step1: Decomped FUN_006125E0 (1762 bytes) - turns out to be a dirty-flag broadcaster with 11 tracked fields at offsets +0x8, +0x24, +0x34, +0xa4, +0xd4, +0x154, +0x1c4, +0x504, +0x554, +0x568, +0x714.
method.step2: Each tracked field has the pattern: if (dirty_bit_2 set) { apply changes, clear bit 2 }; if (init_bit_1 not set) { FUN_007CE7B0(opcode, &flag, 4); set bit 1 }. So each field broadcasts an opcode exactly once (on first access) plus on every apply.
method.step3: Decomped sole caller FUN_006140C0 (276 bytes) - per-frame state apply routine called from 6 places in the FUN_0061XXXX range. Touches param_1+0x118->+0x64->+0x470 chain (deep nested object access).
method.step4: Confirmed FUN_007CE7B0 receives actor_id via `*(this+0xDC)`. The 'this' (ECX) is set by FUN_006125E0's caller chain; not visible in the decomp directly. All 11 opcode broadcasts within one FUN_006125E0 invocation target the SAME actor (ECX set once).

key_findings: FUN_006125E0 is a dirty-flag broadcaster - over-broadcasts opcodes 0x19..0x23 in sequence regardless of whether the receiver handles each one.
All 11 opcodes target the SAME actor (caller sets ECX once before invoking FUN_006125E0).

The element-vtable8-bulk pass found GameManagerElement::vftable[8] (FUN_0055DA80, 33 bytes complete) only implements cases 0x19 and 0x1A. Cases 0x1B..0x21 fall through to the implicit no-op default return.

Resolution: The 7 unmatched opcodes are NOT consumed by any Element class - they are silently dropped by the receiver. This is either (a) forward-compat where the producer was written for a future GameManagerElement variant, or (b) vestigial 1.x state where features were stripped from the receiver but not the producer.

param_1+0x568 -> 0x22 and param_1+0x714 -> 0x23 ARE handled by the element-vtable8-bulk pass (MapLayoutElement cases 0x22 and 0x23 exist in FUN_0059E660). So 0x22/0x23 are also broadcast by this producer but go to MapLayoutElement instead of GameManagerElement, contradicting the 'all same actor' theory above.

RECONCILIATION: GameManagerElement's actor_id may be 0 (zone-level/broadcast) - FUN_004D9910 returning 0 means no actor, and `if (piVar6 != (int *)0x0)` in FUN_004DAA10 skips the dispatch. So opcodes for actor_id=0 are no-op'd by the queue drainer. The 0x22/0x23 opcodes that DO reach MapLayoutElement go through a different actor lookup path (queue entry has a non-zero actor_id for those).
